analysis: The code snippet calls `resourceBundle.getString(key)`. According to the javadoc, this method may throw NullPointerException (if key is null), MissingResourceException (if no object found), and ClassCastException (if the found object is not a string). The code only catches MissingResourceException. There is no null check for `key` before the call, so if key is null, NullPointerException will be thrown uncaught. Similarly, if the resource bundle returns an object that is not a string, ClassCastException will be thrown uncaught. MissingResourceException is caught and handled, so it is avoided. Therefore, the exceptions that are not avoided are NullPointerException and ClassCastException.
answer: NullPointerException: throwing condition not avoided (no null check). ClassCastException: throwing condition not avoided (no type check). MissingResourceException: throwing condition avoided (caught).
remark: NullPointerException is triggered if the `key` parameter is null when passed to `getString`. ClassCastException is triggered if the resource bundle contains an object for the given key that is not a String (e.g., an Integer). Both exceptions are uncaught in the provided code snippet.
